input.question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?
input.ground_truth: Certainly if one considers the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid empire as the "end of antiquity" and the beginning of the early medieval era. It is the last great war because the next one defined the end of the era. Then the question becomes is the Muslim conquest of the Sassanid Empire the best delimiting event between late antiquity and early medieval. There's a lot of good points stating that it is, since the fall of the Sassanid empire meant the Byzantine Empire was then the only surviving great power from classical antiquity. All of the other powers of the era are relatively new. The Muslim conquest of North Africa and Levant also split off those regions from what the classical Roman world. A parallel can be drawn to how the fall of the Soviet Union marked the end of the cold war.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: Was James Howard-Johnston justified in describing the war between Heraclius and Khusro II (602-628) as ‘the last great war of antiquity’?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let's imagine you have a big box of old toys from when your grandparents were little. These toys are special because they're from "the old days," before a lot of the toys you have now.

Now, imagine two big kids, let's call them Heraclius and Khusro, decide they don't like each other and have a huge fight over who gets to play with the best toys in the whole neighborhood. This fight is really, really big and lasts for a long time. Lots of people get involved, and it changes a lot of things.

James Howard-Johnston, who is like a grown-up toy historian, said this fight (the war between Heraclius and Khusro) was "the last great war of antiquity." That means he thinks it was the biggest and most important fight from the old days before everything changed to become the "middle ages" (which is like a new kind of time for toys and people).

He called it that because after this war, the world started to look very different. The big old empires (like the Roman and Persian ones) got weaker, and new kinds of countries and ways of living started to appear. So, this war was almost like the last big hurrah for the old way of doing things.

So, in simple words: James called this war "the last great war of antiquity" because it was one of the biggest, most important fights in the old world, and after it, everything changed to something new. He thought it was a good way to say goodbye to the old times.
